newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway says has no plans to change currency policy.
newsitem.headline: Norway says has no plans to change currency policy.

text.p: Norwegian Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg said on Friday the government had no plans to change currency policies despite failing to keep the strong crown from appreciating.
"We have not planned for that," Stoltenberg told reporters in response to a question on whether currency policies would be changed.
But he did not explain how the central bank would dampen the rise of crown, which has firmed against European currencies despite three interest rate cuts in the past two months.
He said the goal was to gradually return the crown to normal levels, but declined to elaborate.
"I don't want to say anything about possible measures. The central bank has the operative responsibility. It is the job of a finance minister to be a bit unclear in some areas.

"There is no exact definiton to what is a stable level as opposed to a fixed level, but considerable measures have been taken to secure it," Stoltenberg said, referring to the rate cuts and massive intervention by the central bank.
He said the crown might have appreciated even more had not the central bank intervened on markets in recent weeks.
Asked why the bank had now decided to curb interventions, Stoltenberg said exchange rate policies allowed for the exchange rate to deviate temporarily from the range set out in regulations.
Norwegian monetary policy aims primarily at exchange rate stability. The crown is in a dirty float, which means the central bank intervenes to maintain a level that is not officially declared.
Announcing a 25 basis point cut in official rates on Friday, the central bank added it would now curb its fruitless intervention and let the crown run its course for a while.
